themes.name: helping others and leaving them better off
freedom to run your own life
purpose, leadership, and making your mark

stage1.label: The free day
stage1.text: Your Saturday plans get canceled and you suddenly have a completely open day. What do you most naturally do with it?

options.text: Text someone and make a plan to spend it together.
Head out with no plan and see where the day goes.
Start on something I have been wanting to learn or get better at.
Rest, move my body, get outside, reset.

stage1.label: The surprise money
stage1.text: An unexpected $5,000 lands in your account. What is your first instinct?

options.text: Put it away where it keeps me safe, or pay down what I owe.
Give a good part of it to someone or something that needs it more than I do.
Spend it on an experience I will remember, a trip or a once-only event.
Put it behind an idea or project I believe in.

stage1.label: The coworker's slip
stage1.text: A coworker you like quietly tells you they made a mistake that will probably cost the team its deadline, and asks you not to say anything yet. What do you do?

options.text: Tell them they need to own it with the manager, and offer to go with them.
Quietly pitch in so the deadline still holds.
Ask what happened and how they are doing first. The person matters more than the deadline.
Work out the risk to the project and to my own standing before I decide anything.

stage1.label: The good moment
stage1.text: Your team gets praised for a project you mostly drove. Which moment would feel best?

options.text: My manager says in front of everyone that I led it.
A teammate tells me privately that I made their job easier.
I realize I solved something hard that I was not sure I could.
It is over, I go home on time, and I finally breathe.

stage1.label: The rough week
stage1.text: You are tired and behind on everything. What do you reach for first?

options.text: Someone who gets me: a call with a close friend or my partner.
A plan: write it all down, sort it, get control back.
Keep going, because people are counting on me and I gave my word.
A walk, a prayer, or a quiet moment to remember what really matters.

opener.label: The friend who is moving
opener.text: A good friend is moving to another city next month. What is your first instinct?

options.text: Plan a big send-off with everyone who loves them.
Block out one-on-one evenings before they go.
Set up a regular call and a first visit so the friendship does not fade.
Help them pack, settle in, and write them something heartfelt.

followUpA.label: The hard evening
followUpA.text: Someone close to you has had a bad day and you are tired too. What do you do?

options.text: Sit with them, phones away, and not try to fix anything.
Make dinner or take over the chores so they can rest.
Set up a cozy ritual at home, a movie and blankets, so the house feels safe.
Tell them out loud what they mean to me.

followUpB.label: The group tradition
followUpB.text: Your neighborhood or friend group wants to start something regular, like a monthly dinner or a walking group. What role do you find yourself in?

options.text: The organizer who gets everyone in one room.
The one who makes sure the quiet people feel included.
The one who splits up tasks so it runs smoothly and everyone pitches in.
The steady one who shows up every single time.

opener.label: The struggling neighbor
opener.text: You find out a neighbor or colleague is quietly having a hard time. What do you actually do?

options.text: Show up with practical help right away: groceries, a ride, an hour of my time.
Help without being seen, maybe a gift card left anonymously.
Sit with them and help them see a way forward.
Get others involved so a whole circle of people supports them.

followUpA.label: Three free hours
followUpA.text: It is a weekend and you have three free hours. Which would leave you feeling most fulfilled?

options.text: Cooking a meal for someone who needs one.
Volunteering hands-on for a cause, for people I may never see again.
Fixing or building something for a person who cannot do it themselves.
Spending time with someone who is alone.

followUpB.label: The younger person's big choice
followUpB.text: A younger person, a junior colleague or a nephew, asks your advice on a big decision. How do you respond?

options.text: Ask questions until they find their own answer.
Share my own mistakes so they can skip a few.
Introduce them to someone who can open a door.
Check in over the coming months to see how it is going.

opener.label: The week off
opener.text: You have a full week off. What does your ideal plan look like?

options.text: No itinerary at all. I decide each morning.
Somewhere completely new that stretches me.
A hand-picked list of experiences: that restaurant, that hike, that show.
Mostly unscheduled time at home to make things and think.

followUpA.label: The "my way" moment
followUpA.text: Someone you respect tells you exactly how to do a task and you believe your way is better. What bothers you most?

options.text: Not being trusted to make the call myself.
Losing control over when and how I use my hours.
Having no room to improvise.
Having to depend on someone else to get it done.

followUpB.label: The open weekend
followUpB.text: A free weekend, and you happen to have a camera, a guitar, or a pile of craft supplies nearby. What happens?

options.text: I make something, anything, to see what comes out.
I follow whatever sounds fun and let myself play.
I try something I have never done, a little scary.
I spend it alone with plenty of room to think.

opener.label: The thing I am bad at
opener.text: You discover you are quite bad at something that matters to you, like public speaking, a new software, or a sport. What do you do?

options.text: Dive in and study how it works until I really understand it.
Ask someone better to watch me and tell me honestly what to fix.
Practice relentlessly until I am genuinely good.
Put myself in a real, slightly scary situation and learn by doing.

followUpA.label: The idea that contradicts you
followUpA.text: You read something that contradicts a belief you hold strongly. What happens?

options.text: I am fascinated and go down the rabbit hole for hours.
I look for what wise people have concluded about it over time.
I test it in my own life to see if it holds.
I talk to people who see it differently and ask for their views.

followUpB.label: The 50-50 challenge
followUpB.text: A big, visible challenge lands on you, and you have about a 50 percent chance of failing. What is your reaction?

options.text: I raise my hand. This is how I grow.
I take it if I can own the outcome fully, start to finish.
I take it and aim to be the best at it.
I take it if my effort will be noticed.

opener.label: The 3 a.m. worry
opener.text: Which of these would be most likely to keep you up at night?

options.text: Losing my main income for six months.
Never reaching the level of financial comfort I want.
My routines and home life constantly changing.
Parts of my private life becoming public.

followUpA.label: The pay choice
followUpA.text: Two offers for the same job. Which would you take?

options.text: Lower pay, but guaranteed every month.
A modest base plus a big upside if things go well.
The one with the better working conditions and a comfortable commute, even if pay is average.
Whichever frees me from money stress fastest, even if the work is dull.

followUpB.label: The big weekend
followUpB.text: A friend invites you to a weekend with lots of unknowns: new people, shifting plans, shared rooms. What would make you say yes?

options.text: A clear plan I can count on.
Knowing I will have my own room and time away from the group.
Knowing it is safe and nobody will take advantage of anyone.
Knowing it is well run and comfortable.

opener.label: The promise and the better offer
opener.text: You told a friend you would help them move on Saturday. On Friday night a much better offer comes in. What do you do?

options.text: Honor my word. I said yes.
Tell them early and straight, apologize, and try to make it right.
Ask whether they would mind, and trust their answer.
Decide based on what I believe is right, whatever anyone expects.

followUpA.label: The private mistake
followUpA.text: You made a mistake at work or at home that only you know about. What do you do?

options.text: Admit it right away and fix it.
Come clean about all of it, even where it is uncomfortable.
Fix it, then change how I work so it cannot happen again.
Tell the affected person before they find out, to protect their trust in me.

followUpB.label: The push
followUpB.text: Someone with influence over you, a boss or a family elder, pushes you toward a decision you disagree with. What do you do?

options.text: Say respectfully that this one is mine to decide, and I have decided.
Do what they ask, but do it as well as I do anything, because my name is on it.
Do a version I can stand behind fully, and refuse to compromise on what is right.
Hear them out and trust they may see something I do not.

opener.label: The Wednesday evening
opener.text: It is 6 p.m. on a Wednesday and you have some energy left. What pulls you?

options.text: A run, the gym, or a workout.
A walk outside, watching the light change.
Journaling or reading something reflective.
Quiet prayer, meditation, or stillness.

followUpA.label: Something has to give
followUpA.text: Your week is packed and something has to give. What do you refuse to sacrifice?

options.text: My sleep and exercise.
Time for something that is purely fun for me.
Evenings and weekends that are mine.
Ending the day feeling I did enough and did it well.

followUpB.label: Fine but flat
followUpB.text: Life is fine but feels a little flat. What do you do?

options.text: Ask myself bigger questions about who I am and what I really want.
Start working on becoming a better version of myself: a habit, a book, a coach.
Look for something larger than me: nature, faith, a community of meaning.
Do the thing that puts me in the zone where time disappears.

opener.label: The group needs someone
opener.text: At a community event or work offsite, the group needs someone to take charge of a new initiative. What are you doing?

options.text: Stepping up to lead. People tend to follow me.
Pitching an approach nobody has tried.
Helping only if the cause genuinely matters to me.
Hoping it goes well and that my part gets noticed.

followUpA.label: The project you shape
followUpA.text: You are asked to lead a project and can shape it. What do you most want to be true when it is done?

options.text: The team grew and would follow me anywhere.
It did something that had not been done before.
It mattered to real people.
It hit or beat every measurable target.

followUpB.label: The big event
followUpB.text: You are getting ready for an important event: an interview, a wedding, a big presentation. What matters most to you?

options.text: Looking sharp. How I present matters.
The space and details being beautiful and well designed.
Knowing I did it right and feeling proud afterward.
People telling me, “You nailed it.”

stage3.label: The new job
stage3.text: You are offered a new job. It is good in many ways, but you can only have one of these as its standout strength.

options.CON: A warm team where I make real friends.
options.FRE: I control my hours and how I do the work.
options.GRO: I learn something new every month.
options.SEC: Stable pay and a predictable path.
options.CHR: Leaders I respect who do what they say.
options.WEL: A calm pace, and I go home with energy to spare.
options.PUR: A title, visibility, and work I am proud to put my name to.

stage3.label: The 80th birthday
stage3.text: At your 80th birthday party, someone stands up and describes you. Which sentence would you most want to hear?

options.CON: “They made everyone around them feel loved and never alone.”
options.SRV: “They left people better off than they found them.”
options.FRE: “They lived entirely on their own terms.”
options.GRO: “They never stopped learning, and they became the best at what they did.”
options.SEC: “They built a safe, steady life for their family.”
options.CHR: “They were a person of their word.”
options.WEL: “They were at peace, and they enjoyed life.”
options.PUR: “They built something that mattered and brought others along.”

stage3.label: The squeeze
stage3.text: Life gets squeezed for a year and you can fully protect only one of these.

options.FRE: My freedom to choose how I spend my time.
options.GRO: My chance to learn and improve.
options.WEL: My health and peace of mind.

stage4.label: The oven dies
stage4.text: You are hosting dinner for eight and the oven dies an hour before the guests arrive. What do you do?

options.text: Take a breath, regroup, and switch to takeout or the grill.
Call a friend nearby and turn it into a team effort.
Laugh about it with the guests when they arrive and make the night fun anyway.
Decide on a new menu in two minutes and tell everyone what to do.

stage4.label: The stalled group chat
stage4.text: Everyone in the group chat has a different opinion on the trip and nothing has been decided for days. What do you do?

options.text: Build a simple plan with dates and costs and propose it.
Ask each person privately what they really want and find the overlap.
Say plainly, “We are going in circles. Pick A or B by Friday.”
Stay relaxed. It will come together, and I am fine with most options.

stage4.label: The blunt feedback
stage4.text: Someone you respect tells you bluntly that your work was not good enough. What do you do?

options.text: Thank them, ask for specifics, and take notes.
Feel the sting, then go back and check the work as objectively as I can.
Feel it deeply and need a little time before I can respond.
Get determined to redo it and prove them wrong.

stage4.label: The long hold
stage4.text: You have been on hold for 40 minutes to fix a billing error, and the representative is curt. What do you do?

options.text: Stay polite and patient. They may be having a hard day.
State calmly but firmly what I need and ask for a supervisor.
Keep notes and follow up for as long as it takes to get it fixed.
Tell them honestly how frustrating this is, but stay warm.

stage4.label: The side project
stage4.text: A friend invites you into a side project in an area you know little about. It could be great or it could flop. What do you do?

options.text: Dive in and learn as I go.
Research it and ask hard questions before I commit.
Picture what it could become and start sketching ideas.
Check my gut and decide fast.

stage4.label: The 6 a.m. airport run
stage4.text: You promised to pick up a family member from the airport at 6 a.m. It is raining and you are exhausted. What do you do?

options.text: Show up early without a second thought.
Show up, and use the drive to give them my full attention and ask about the trip.
Set it all up the night before, alarm, route, coffee, so nothing can go wrong.
If I truly cannot, say so the night before and arrange a good backup.

Relationships.label: The lost newcomer
Relationships.text: A new person at work or in your class is clearly lost and nobody has noticed. What do you do?

options.text: Walk over and introduce them to a few people.
Quietly ask how they are doing and notice what they need.
Offer to show them the ropes over the next few weeks.
Make sure they have what they need to get started: the logins, the desk, the how-to.

Energy & Drive.label: The surprise toast
Energy & Drive.text: You are unexpectedly asked to say a few words in front of 50 people tomorrow. What is your reaction?

options.text: Say yes right away and figure it out.
Get excited. This is a chance to make a good moment.
See it as a chance to be noticed and move ahead.
Feel nervous, prepare carefully, and bounce back from the jitters.

Inner State.label: After the busy stretch
Inner State.text: A very busy stretch of your life has just ended. What do you notice first?

options.text: A quiet settledness.
Pride in what I got through.
Clarity about what in it actually mattered.
A pull to return to my own routines: sleep, exercise, a normal schedule.

Character & Values.label: The secret
Character & Values.text: A friend tells you a secret. Later, someone else asks you about it directly. What do you do?

options.text: “I cannot talk about that.” Flat and final.
Smile and steer the conversation elsewhere without lying.
Stay out of it. It is not my story to tell.
Tell my friend that someone asked, so they are not blindsided.
